exposures.snippet: On Polymarket, traders put the most weight on a first-day closing value of $1.2 to $1.5 trillion.

rationale: Reference class: large private tech company with no public filing, listing on one named day; base rate 0.03 from memory. Evidence: the public S-1 was filed Oct 26, the price range was set Nov 10, and reports expect pricing Nov 18 with trading Nov 19, which is the day before this question's Nov 20 date. Strongest argument against a low number is that a slip of one day would still make it Yes only if the listing lands on Nov 20 exactly, so I put it at 0.08. The market-price exposure was discarded and did not set this number.

Reference class: the current largest company by market cap still holding the top spot about two weeks later; base rate 0.75 from memory. Evidence: mid-November reports (Motley Fool, Nov 13) rank Apple first, with Nvidia second by roughly $129B at the Nov 12 close, and older pages still showing Nvidia first are outdated. That moves Nvidia from the holder case to a near-second challenger case, so 0.3 is well outside the 15-point band, justified by the new evidence. Strongest argument against: sources conflict on the current order, and a small gap can reverse in two weeks.

Reference class: formal mutually agreed general ceasefire in a major interstate war within a two-week window; base rate 0.04 from memory. Evidence: the Nov 10-11 Abu Dhabi trilateral talks produced only a prisoner-exchange deal in principle, Russia has said it will not accept short-term ceasefires, and territory (Donbas) remains blocked. Zelensky's possible meeting with Putin is planned for December, after this window. Strongest argument against: US-mediated talks are active, so a surprise framework could be announced, but the stated positions do not support it by Nov 30.

Reference class: a US funding lapse beginning in a mid-fiscal-year month, not at Oct 1; base rate 0.05 from memory of about 20 lapses since 1980. Evidence: an enacted continuing resolution (P.L. 119-103) funds the government through December 11, 2026, so no lapse can start in November under current law. This is a nearly settled case, so 0.01 is justified. Strongest argument against: the market's own wording says it resolves on any lapse during November, and an unexpected early shutdown would require a legal change, which is very unlikely.

Reference class: a named frontier AI model released within a short window before a deadline with no announced date; base rate 0.08 from memory. Evidence: searches found no Anthropic announcement of a Fable 5.5 and no confirmed release date; the rumored release that was predicted for the week of the leaks did not happen. One November source reports a Fable 5.2 release on Nov 9, which is unverified and is a different version name. Strongest argument against: leak-driven launches can come with little notice, but the window closes in two days.

Reference class: a compound, loosely specified AI-lab announcement with several conjoined claims within about two weeks; base rate 0.05 from rough judgment, with no reliable count. Evidence: a search found no OpenAI announcement of a massively recursive model, a mechinterp system, or non-token pricing, and the pricing sources report no change in token rates. The market resolves by a private bet outcome, which I cannot check. Strongest argument against: OpenAI has been making large announcements, and the conjunction could be met by loose wording.

Reference class: a commodity front-month price touching a level about 40 percent or more above spot within one month; base rate 0.03 from memory, but that assumed spot far below $100. Evidence: WTI settled about $88.5 on Nov 13, so $100 is roughly 13 percent above, and the 52-week range reaching about $113-118 shows high volatility. Against it, the IEA reports a supply surplus and prices have fallen two weeks running. The high-volatility touch estimate is roughly 0.15-0.2, so I set 0.12, well outside the base-rate band because the current price was found to be much closer. Strongest argument against: the surplus trend and falling prices.

Reference class: a specific named next-version AI model made publicly available within a two-week window with no announced date; base rate 0.05 from memory of a few dozen launches. Evidence: GPT-6 Astra launched Sept 3, 2026, so the 6.1 designation is the next step, but no announcement of a 6.1 Astra was found. One aggregator page titled 'GPT-6.1 Sol & Astra' suggests a version exists, but it is unverified and is not an OpenAI source, so I raised the number only slightly to 0.08. Strongest argument against: if a 6.1 Astra already exists and is public, the question would resolve Yes.

Reference class: formal announcement of a named individual's appointment to a major international post in a given month with no reported process; base rate 0.03 from memory. Evidence: Reuters (Oct 15) reported, citing four sources, that the WEF could appoint Lagarde as early as November, with a board meeting on Nov 2 as a possible date, though the board might instead vote in January. I found no report of an outcome from Nov 2. Strongest argument against: the report was from October, the vote may not have happened, and the board could push the decision to January.

rationale: Reference class: a large private tech company with no public filing, listed by a near-term cutoff; base rate 0.02 from memory. Evidence: the S-1 is public, the amended filing set the range at $70-78, the roadshow began Nov 10, the book is reported as covered, and reports say pricing on Nov 18 with trading on Nov 19, within the window. The date depends on regulatory clearance and market conditions, so I did not go higher. Strongest argument against: any slip past Nov 19 resolves No. The market-price exposure was discarded and did not set this number.

exposures.snippet: On Polymarket, traders put the most weight on a first-day closing value of $1.2 to $1.5 trillion.

rationale: Reference class: a large private tech company with no public filing, listed by a cutoff about a week later; base rate 0.03 from memory. Evidence: the scheduled trading start of Nov 19 is six days before this Nov 25 cutoff, with the range set and the book reported covered. The gap leaves room for a one-week slip. Strongest argument against: a delay of more than six days, for example from regulatory clearance or a market sell-off, resolves No. The market-price exposure was discarded and did not set this number.

Reference class: a frontier AI lab claiming a solved Clay Millennium Prize problem before a set date; base rate 0.01 from memory, since no Millennium problem has been solved to date. Evidence: the Navier-Stokes rumor about Anthropic was not supported and was disputed, Terence Tao said he never claimed it, and no Anthropic proof has been published. OpenAI's own Navier-Stokes claim is a different lab and does not count here. Strongest argument against: a loosely worded Anthropic statement about partial progress could be read as a claim, but the question excludes weaker variants.
